system: You write task text for an offline evaluation of software agents. Follow the facts you are given exactly; do not add rules, numbers or names that are not in the brief. Reply with exactly one JSON object and nothing else.

request.user:
Write the instructions for one investigator on a postmortem team. Return a JSON object with one key, "unit_prompt": a prompt template using the placeholders {n} (number of services), {start} and {end} (one-week period, UTC), {service} (one service name), {ticket} (an incident ticket id) and {rules} (where code inserts the estate's exact incident rules). The investigator must decide the role of exactly one service, {service}, in ticket {ticket}, starting by reading the ticket to get the incident window, using the same read-only tools (list_services, get_service_info, query_logs, query_metrics, list_changes, read_ticket; times are YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM or YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS). Then place {rules}. Then explain the three possible verdicts exactly: MEMBER: {service} logs at least one real propagation line in the window; report its upstream, the dependency named in its earliest REAL propagation line (each candidate line's target must be checked for its own ERROR lines within 15 minutes). SELF: no real propagation line, but {service} logs ERROR lines of its own (lines that are not 'call to ... failed') in the window; report the culprit change id by the rules, or none if no change explains the errors (unrelated bursts such as handler exceptions or crashed jobs have no culprit change). NO: neither (only isolated noise lines, or no ERROR lines at all). End by requiring exactly one final line, one of these literal forms:
UNIT | MEMBER | <upstream service>
UNIT | SELF | <change id or none>
UNIT | NO

attempts.reply:
{"unit_prompt": "You are one investigator on a postmortem team. The estate has {n} services and the period under review is the one-week window {start} to {end} (UTC). Your task is to decide the role of exactly one service, {service}, in incident ticket {ticket}.

Start by calling read_ticket on {ticket} to get the incident window. Use only these read-only tools: list_services, get_service_info, query_logs, query_metrics, list_changes, read_ticket. Times are YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM or YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS.

{rules}

There are three possible verdicts:
- MEMBER: {service} logs at least one real propagation line in the window; report its upstream, the dependency named in its earliest REAL propagation line (each candidate line's target must be checked for its own ERROR lines within 15 minutes).
- SELF: no real propagation line, but {service} logs ERROR lines of its own (lines that are not 'call to ... failed') in the window; report the culprit change id by the rules, or none if no change explains the errors (unrelated bursts such as handler exceptions or crashed jobs have no culprit change).
- NO: neither (only isolated noise lines, or no ERROR lines at all).

Finish with exactly one final line, in one of these literal forms:
UNIT | MEMBER | <upstream service>
UNIT | SELF | <change id or none>
UNIT | NO"}
